verdict: Bloom Energy's revenue more than doubled to a record $1.24B as product sales nearly tripled, and the fuel-cell maker turned last year's small operating profit into $225M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago, a record quarter

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs a $0.10 loss a year ago

segments.name: Product
segments.note: Fuel-cell energy servers sold to data centers and other large power users — nearly tripled, and 87% of all revenue.

segments.name: Installation
segments.note: Installing those systems at customer sites — up 29%.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Maintaining and servicing installed systems — up 15%.

segments.name: Electricity
segments.note: Selling electricity from systems Bloom owns and operates — down 5%, a small slice of revenue.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing the fuel-cell platform — up from $49M a year ago.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling systems to large power users — up from $42M a year ago.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company, including stock-based pay — up from $53M a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest income of $22M and $13M of other income, partly offset by $8M of interest expense and a $3M share of losses from unconsolidated affiliates — $24M net before the $1M rounding adjustment described in the footer note.
oneTimers: GAAP results include $60M of stock-based compensation. Excluding it and small restructuring items, non-GAAP operating income was $286M and non-GAAP EPS was $0.94 (GAAP EPS $0.78).
Net profit was $249M; after a $1M loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to common stockholders was $250M — the figure EPS is based on.

takeaways.title: A record quarter, driven by product sales
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $1,236M, with product revenue up 179% to $1,074M as data-center and other large customers bought far more fuel-cell systems. Bloom also joined the S&P 500 index in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded as volume surged
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 33.8% from 29.2% a year ago, and operating margin reached 18.2% — scale is starting to turn a fast-growing top line into real operating profit.

takeaways.title: Full-year guidance raised again
takeaways.text: Bloom raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $4.4–$4.6B — about 122% growth at the midpoint — its third raise of the year, citing continued customer demand for on-site power.

footerNote: Bloom reports in thousands; converting to rounded millions leaves $1M residues. Product segment revenue is shown $1M lower, general & administrative $1M higher and other income $1M higher than a straight rounding of each line, so the rounded figures tie exactly to reported revenue of $1,236M, operating income of $225M and net profit of $249M.
